paragraphs.source_en: Uan Afuda shelter presents a human occupation from the Epipalaeolithic until the Pastoral periods. Besides the microlithic industry, grinding stones and remains of wild fauna, the oldest level, dating at around 9,200 BP, includes a simple stone structure suggesting a possible dwelling. Important for the interpretation of the site is the Mesolithic layer dating at around 8,000 BP, made of a massive accumulation of dung attributed to mouflon (Ammotragus lervia). Di Lernia (1999; 2001) believes that Mesolithic groups occupying the cave kept mouflon in an attempt to tame them. The fact that the mouflon there were fed with a toxic plant is examined later. The function of this shelter could therefore have been occupational with the eventual keeping of wild mouflon for subsistence.
